purpose: Reduce render workload while moving through the expanded university and moat scene; investigate the apparent 60 FPS limit.

baseline.description: The already-dirty working tree saved at task start, not Git HEAD. Only runtime source files change in this task.

implementation.grouping: Whole low silhouette when the region is distant and more than eight low cells intersect either eye; otherwise local cells. Shared low attributes, separate indices and exact local bounds.
implementation.culling: Transformed cell AABBs for view and shadow frustums.
implementation.shadow: Independent static low cell casters; no whole-proxy casting or duplicate near/proxy view draws.
implementation.projection: debugView now updates its projection for each requested FOV. The baseline receives the identical diagnostic correction in browser routing.

methodology: Same Chrome page, 1280 x 720, device scale 1, reduced motion, benchmark=1 disables adaptive resolution.

The delivered 96/128 m campus/moat grid uses a four-view comparison, before then after. The prior 64/96 m candidate has a six-view after/before pair and a two-view before/after repeat, retained separately.
Each view settles 2.5 seconds, then the ordinary probe excludes two seconds of warmup and samples for eight seconds.
CPU render/GPU query summaries include warmup and sampling; they are not the identical interval to the delivered-frame probe.
GPU queries are asynchronous EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2; no finish/wait is used. Disjoint query results are discarded.
The prior WebGL renderer/context is disposed before navigating between revisions. No test/build process runs during measurement.
FOV and projection entries verify identical requested cameras in the final comparison and reversed repeat.
limits: Host performance varies sharply: CPU speed limit was 55 near setup and later 22, with scheduler limit 40. No recorded thermal warning is not evidence of unthrottled GPU clocks.

Earlier six-view timings mix throttled and refresh-limited periods. Do not attribute their large FPS changes solely to source code. Even the earlier reversed repeat has worse after-change p95 frame cadence despite lower GPU medians; the delivered grid uses larger cells to reduce CPU submissions.
A different application was active on the host. Its processes were observed and left untouched; exclusive CPU/GPU ownership is not established.
Frame cadence remains browser/display controlled. No application-level 60 FPS limiter exists. No 120/144 Hz display was tested.
Resident geometry counts deduplicate shared attributes and indices; these are not total VRAM or peak memory.
Loading time, transfer counts, texture allocation order and retained-heap changes are not established by source routing and warm sequential viewpoints.
No real phone, VR headset or battery measurement.

verification.controllerTimings: Synthetic fixed-step route traversals overlap the final regression run; controller timing fields are diagnostic only, not an isolated CPU benchmark.
